reference_method: Independent Pandas imports and calculations; no production expression/parser reused by reference. Explicit human-reviewed evaluation definitions, not runtime mappings.

source.license: NYC TLC public-use trip records; source usage terms apply. Seaborn mirror provides no separate dataset license. Not redistributed in this repository.
source.citation: NYC Taxi & Limousine Commission, March 2019 sample distributed by seaborn-data. Sample selection and modifications are not fully documented; no population inference.

initial_cases.grain: One sampled completed taxi trip, not one rider; repeated riders are not identifiable.

metric.name: Recorded trip total
metric.description: Sum of recorded total charges for selected trips; components are not re-added.
metric.limitations: Sampled observed charges, not profit or city-wide revenue.
metric.compiled_sql: sum(CASE WHEN isfinite(try_cast(NULLIF(trim(CAST("total" AS VARCHAR)),'') AS DOUBLE)) THEN try_cast(NULLIF(trim(CAST("total" AS VARCHAR)),'') AS DOUBLE) END)

findings: Recorded trip total differs by 79,624 USD between credit card and None.
Recorded trip total ranges from 2,249.7 to 4,298.8 USD across observed day periods.
total: the middle half of finite values lies between 11.3 and 20.38.
initial_cases.status: passed API/reference evaluation; browser evaluation recorded separately

histogram_reference.reference: Independent NumPy histogram with the documented separate exact-maximum boundary bin.

exploratory_segmentation.limitations: Exploratory standardized Euclidean k-means, fixed seed; clusters are model-generated groups, not verified personas or business truth. The silhouette score uses at most 2,000 deterministically sampled fitted rows; it is an internal score, not external validation. Confirm one independent entity per row; repeated transactions can cluster activity instead of customers. Features, outliers and k affect results. The two-dimensional SVD view is a projection, not the full clustering geometry.

source.license: R datasets package: GPL-2 or GPL-3; source documentation and attribution retained locally. No raw data redistributed in repository.
source.citation: R airquality, Chambers et al. (1983); daily New York observations May–September 1973. Ozone Roosevelt Island, other measurements at different stations; no city-wide exposure estimate.
source.derivation: Lossless Parquet conversion plus documented constant year 1973; original CSV preserved.

initial_cases.grain: One calendar day with station-specific measurements; unavailable measurements are missing, not zero.

metric.name: Mean observed ozone
metric.description: Arithmetic mean over finite available ozone measurements.
metric.limitations: 37 days lack ozone; stations differ by measure and source coverage is limited.
metric.compiled_sql: avg(CASE WHEN isfinite(try_cast(NULLIF(trim(CAST("Ozone" AS VARCHAR)),'') AS DOUBLE)) THEN try_cast(NULLIF(trim(CAST("Ozone" AS VARCHAR)),'') AS DOUBLE) END)

findings: Mean observed ozone differs by 36.346 ppb between 8 and 5.
Mean observed ozone ranges from 23.615 to 59.962 ppb across observed month periods.
Ozone: the middle half of finite values lies between 18 and 63.25.
Ozone: 24.2% of selected rows are missing.

confidence_interval.assumptions: Independent observations, representative sampling and a reasonably well-behaved sampling distribution. Repeated entities, strong skew at small n and selection bias can invalidate this interval. It does not correct nonrepresentative data.

welch_reference.assumptions: Welch two-sided independent-group mean comparison. Review independence, repeated entities, outliers, sampling bias and skew. A small p-value is not proof of practical importance or causality. This is one planned comparison; adjust p-values when screening many comparisons.

initial_cases.forecast_guard: Forecasting currently supports additive sum/count monthly metrics only.

source.citation: Wickham, nycflights13; source RITA/Bureau of Transportation Statistics, NYC departures in 2013. Rdatasets mirror, not an independently acquired BTS extract.

initial_cases.grain: One scheduled NYC departure record in 2013; flight number alone is not unique.

metric.name: Recorded arrival delay
metric.description: Mean over finite recorded arrival delays; negative values are early arrivals.
metric.limitations: Missing arrival delay is excluded; this is not a cancellation rate.
metric.compiled_sql: avg(CASE WHEN isfinite(try_cast(NULLIF(trim(CAST("arr_delay" AS VARCHAR)),'') AS DOUBLE)) THEN try_cast(NULLIF(trim(CAST("arr_delay" AS VARCHAR)),'') AS DOUBLE) END)

findings: Recorded arrival delay differs by 31.852 minutes between F9 and AS.
Recorded arrival delay ranges from -4.0184 to 16.711 minutes across observed month periods.
arr_delay: the middle half of finite values lies between -17 and 14.
